label: Packing ratio
source: Hardy 1996 PNW-GTR-364: machine piles 0.06-0.26; 0.20 short-needle conifer default, 0.25 compacted loader piles

label: Wood density (dry)
source: Sierra mixed conifer specific gravity ~0.34-0.45

label: Lidar volume adjustment
source: Measured sampling error ~+/-7% for piles over 40 ft; bias from rough tops, ground disturbance and toe cutoff not measured

label: Diesel price
source: AAA California average diesel, Oct 24, 2026: $8.46/gal (on-road retail, taxes included). Changes only the fuel share of each rate, using the fuel use below. Grinder, carbonator and their loaders pay the dyed off-road price worked out from it with the taxes below; chip vans, lowboys and fire support pay this price

label: Diesel price in the default rates
source: Assumed: the default rates were set when California diesel was about $5 (AAA average $5.12 on Oct 24, 2025)

label: California diesel excise
source: CDTFA, Jul 2026-Jun 2027: 48.2 cents/gal on diesel except dyed diesel, which pays no excise unless used on highway. Not part of the sales tax base

label: Federal diesel excise
source: 24.4 cents/gal; dyed diesel for off-highway use is exempt (bar the 0.1 cent LUST fee, ignored). Part of the California sales tax base

label: Diesel sales tax
source: CDTFA, Jul 2026-Jun 2027: 13.00% on diesel except dyed diesel, plus district taxes (left out: they apply to both)

label: Dyed diesel sales tax, off-road use
source: CDTFA: dyed diesel used off-road pays the statewide rate, 7.25%, plus district taxes, with a CDTFA-230-R-1 certificate from the buyer

label: Grinder and loader fuel
source: Assumed: ~1,000 hp horizontal grinder ~30-35 gal per productive hour plus grapple loader ~5-8 gal/h

label: Chip van fuel economy
source: Assumed: loaded and empty chip van on mixed forest and highway roads ~5-6 mpg

label: Chip van idling per load
source: Assumed: ~1 h idling at loading and unloading

label: Carbonator and loader fuel
source: Assumed: carbonator engine (fans, hydraulics) ~3-5 gal/h plus feeding loader ~5-7 gal/h

label: Fire support fuel
source: Assumed: water tender and patrol pickup ~20-30 gal per shift

label: Move-in fuel
source: Assumed: lowboy round trips for a machine and its loader, ~100 gal per project move-in

label: Grind and load
source: Central Sierra feedstock report 2023: $50-65/BDT to grind and load chip vans in the forest (grapple loader feeding a horizontal grinder)

label: Grinder output
source: Yoshioka et al. 2017 (Sierra Nevada slash piles): 30.7 BDT per productive hour without delays; ~20 with moves and delays

label: Grinding hours per day
source: Assumed single shift

label: Haul distance one-way
source: Routed road distance from the units to Rio Bravo Rocklin, Lincoln, the nearest operating plant burning forest fuel (pick other destinations above)

label: Average haul speed
source: Routed car time units to Lincoln 2.0 h for 69 mi incl. ~20 mi of forest roads; loaded chip vans ~15% slower; plus 1 h to load and unload per trip

label: Chip van rate
source: Central Sierra 2023: $130-150/h, raised for inflation to 2026

label: Load size
source: Assumed: ~25 field t chip van at ~half moisture

label: Chip vans hauling
source: Assumed: about what keeps one grinder busy on a ~70 mi haul (one round trip per truck per day)

label: Contractor overhead and profit
source: Applied to grind, load and haul (cost basis); carbonator rate already includes it

label: Grinder move-in per project
source: Assumed: lowboy moves for grinder and loader in and out, plus turnaround and access work for chip vans

label: Plant pays (+) or charges (-)
source: CAL FIRE 2023: sellers get $45-50/BDT at best and some loads pay tipping fees; dirty pile grindings may be downgraded, so the default takes no credit

label: Carbonator rate
source: Siskiyou 2020 demo 4.7; Earth Foundries 6050 10-15 green t/h (~6-10 dry); 6040 15-20+ t/h. 10 dry t/h is the top of the 6050 range

label: Productive hours per day
source: Assumed: 10 h shift less warm-up, quench, moves, service

label: Carbonators working
source: Mendocino NF ran three 6040s on one project

label: Carbonator contract rate
source: Siskiyou $847/h all-in 2020-21 incl. feeding loader, + inflation and margin -> ~$1,150-1,300

label: Carbonator move-in per project
source: Assumed: lowboy moves for carbonator and loader in and out

label: Biochar yield
source: Siskiyou 2020 demo: 46.7 t biochar from 373 BDT. Biochar sale value is not credited

label: Fire support per working day
source: Assumed: contracted water tender with operator ~$100-150/h for a 10 h shift in fire season, one per carbonator. Not costed for grinding, where fire support is the Forest Service's own

label: Working days per season
source: Assumed operating window per field season
